headline: Plumbing Fixture Warning Signs: When Hidden Valve and Drain Issues Require a Pro
articleBody:
A dripping faucet or loose toilet handle might seem minor, but plumbing fixtures often display warning signs that point to deeper issues behind the finish. Here is when to call a professional:

- Seized or weeping shutoff valves: If the angle stops under the sink or toilet will not turn, leak when touched, or fail to stop water flow completely, they must be rebuilt or replaced before changing fixtures.
- Spongy flooring around the toilet base: Water seeping past a damaged wax ring or broken closet flange rots subflooring long before dampness is visible on top.
- Low water volume after installation: Sudden drops in pressure often indicate corroded supply risers or sediment dislodged inside older galvanized lines.
- Mismatched shower trim and valve bodies: Modern trim kits rarely fit older rough-in valves from different manufacturers, requiring access behind tile walls.
- Stained ceilings below the bathroom: Hidden drain slip-joint leaks or cracked tub overflow gaskets can quietly rot floor joists.

When Professional Guidance Helps
When you need to adjust behind-the-wall copper or PEX connections, repair damaged floor flanges, or open tile without harming surrounding finishes, a licensed contractor keeps your home protected.
